question: Who was India's first Olympic medalist in wrestling?
solution:
The correct answer is __**K. D. Jadhav**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Khashaba Dadasaheb Jadhav**, often referred to as the **'Pocket Dynamo'**, created history by winning a **bronze medal** in **wrestling** at the **1952 Helsinki Olympics**.
 
• He competed in the **Bantamweight category** (52 kg) of **freestyle wrestling**, defeating wrestlers from Canada, Mexico, Germany, and others to secure his place on the podium.
 
• This achievement made him the **first individual athlete** from **independent India** to win an Olympic medal, a milestone that stood as the only individual medal for India for several decades.
 
• Before his success in 1952, Jadhav also participated in the **1948 London Olympics**, where he finished in **sixth place**, which was highly commendable given he was used to wrestling in **traditional mud pits (Akhada)** rather than mats.
 
• His victory paved the way for future generations of Indian wrestlers, establishing **wrestling** as a primary sport for India on the global stage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sushil Kumar**:

 
 
• He is a legendary Indian wrestler who won a **bronze medal** at the **2008 Beijing Olympics** and a **silver medal** at the **2012 London Olympics**.
 
• He is the only Indian since independence to win **two individual Olympic medals** in an individual sport.
 
 
 
• **Yogeshwar Dutt**:
 
 
• He clinched the **bronze medal** in the **60 kg freestyle** category at the **2012 London Olympics**.
 
• He was awarded the **Padma Shri** and the **Khel Ratna** for his contributions to Indian sports.
 
 
 
• **Bajrang Punia**:
 
 
• A prominent modern-day wrestler who won the **bronze medal** in the **65 kg freestyle** category at the **2020 Tokyo Olympics**.
 
• He is the only Indian wrestler to win **four medals** at the **World Wrestling Championships**.
